NCCL-13 : Network communication through one hop NVLink
Design

$CONTENTS

Proposed Design

We introduce a new type of path in the topology graph, PXN (PCI x NVLink), which goes through another GPU before reaching the NIC. These types of paths can be disabled with NCCL_PXN_DISABLE=1 (default 0).

Contrary to one-hop P2P, we don't use the remote allocator of the intermediate rank, because we cannot use GPU Direct RDMA on CUDA IPC mapped buffers. Hence, when connecting two ranks through PXN, the sender will allocate memory on the intermediate GPU. That requires the intermediate GPU to allow for multiple CUDA contexts, which we check beforehand through a call to wrapNvmlDeviceGetComputeMode and add to the XML data and topology graph.

The PXN paths are not computed during the original path computation as it was easier to do it as a post step, connecting GPU-GPU paths with GPU-NIC paths. This also makes it easier to disable PXN when the CUDA compute mode is not compatible with remote memory allocation.

We add a new field in the GPU information, netDev, which allows each rank to advertise to others which NIC is local. We then use that NIC in two ways: to help GPUs choose which intermediate local GPU they will use to reach a given NIC, and to choose which NIC to use when sending data to a remote rank.

Interface Architecture

A new netDev field is added to the peerInfo struct.

System KPIs & Metrics

Performance on DGX A100 has been measured at 23.6 GB/s on 8 nodes, versus 25.3 GB/s with direct communication.
